text:
marta: quick idea — instead of one big 'spot burst' pool, what if we split bursts into small heterogeneous pools (gpu-small, gpu-large, gpu-preemptible-fast) and route based on job QoS?

devin: can you expand on "heterogeneous pools"? do you mean different instance families / preemption profiles?

marta: yes. each burst pool would be a mix of preemptible types with similar eviction characteristics. we keep a minimal on-demand floor per-AZ for critical low-latency inference. non-critical batch jobs go to the heterogeneous spot pools.

ryan: sounds good. pros: better chance to find capacity when one family is scarce, and we can optimize packing. cons: more autoscaler rules + routing complexity.

jia: routing complexity is the real cost. we should use a QoS tag on pod/job: "latency:critical|best-effort|batch" and let scheduler pick pool. also add a fallback policy: if burst pools are 90% evicted in an AZ, route to on-demand floor in nearest region.

sam: agree. also add a small warm-standby group of on-demand gpus (like 5% of baseline) that we can spin into service faster than cold provisioning — helps with short spikes.

marta: implementation sketch: 1) label nodes pools: pool=burst-small/pool=burst-large/pool=ondemand-floor 2) scheduler uses nodeAffinity + QoS tag 3) fallback controller monitors eviction rate and flips a `prefer_on_demand` flag per-AZ

devin: can we avoid per-AZ state? maybe per-region with weights so we don't get too many knobs. per-AZ needed for networking locality though.

ryan: sample k8s snippet for QoS + affinity:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    app: reranker
    qos: latency-critical
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: pool
            operator: In
            values:
            - ondemand-floor
            - burst-small
```

jia: eviction handling: we should implement graceful drain hooks for critical pods — push a small token to the frontend allowing longer tail latency for a few seconds while we switch to fallback model. push config as feature flag.

ops-bot: [cluster-autoscaler] event: spot eviction spike in us-west-2: 78% of burst-small nodes evicted in last 10m. autoscaler triggered scale-up for ondemand-floor-az-a.

marta: ops-bot — thanks. that's exactly the kind of signal our fallback controller should consume. devin, can you add a consumer to autoscaler events?

devin: yes. i'll add a consumer that emits per-pool eviction_rate and a derived boolean 'eviction_unhealthy'. then fallback controller subscribes. estimate: 2d to prototype.

sam: cost note: if we keep a 5% warm standing on-demand, estimated $12k/mo extra but cuts tail-SLO violations by ~60% in our sim. I'll put numbers in the doc.

ryan: one more constraint — network egress: some regions have lower gpu counts but also limited cross-AZ egress. prefer routing within AZ for high-throughput jobs. fallback should consider egress cap.

jia: agree. also add a cooldown window so we don't flip back-and-forth when spot markets pulse. recommend 10m hold-off after a fallback.

marta: next steps: devin protos eviction consumer + sample scheduler affinity; ryan to run sim with mixed families; sam to run cost/benefit calc; i'll draft a short runbook for oncall with fallback run states.

devin: noted. will start on autoscaler consumer & share PoC channel.

ryan: i'll try 3 mixes: 70/30, 50/50, 30/70 (ondemand/spot) and report p95/p99 for inference SLO.

marta: perfect. if anyone hits a blocker ping me. :rocket:

sam: thanks all. putting numbers in the doc now: https://redwood.internal/roadmaps/heterogeneous-burst (draft)

ops-bot: [notice] Rolling update on ondemand-floor-az-a started (3 nodes replacing).
